desc:
The integer array nums may contain repeated values. Return every distinct subset that has exactly k elements. Two subsets are the same when they hold the same values with the same multiplicities, regardless of which positions the values came from.

Write the values of each subset in non-decreasing order. Rows may be returned in any order. For k = 0 the only subset is the empty one, so the answer is [[]].
hints: First solve it for distinct values: choose k of them with a start index so that each set is produced once.
Sort the array so that equal values are neighbours. Then two choices give the same subset exactly when they take the same number of copies of each value.
Within one loop over candidate positions, skip nums[i] when i > start and nums[i] == nums[i-1]. Also stop when fewer than the needed number of elements remain.
editorial: Sort nums. Recurse on (start, need) with the current list. When need == 0, record a copy. Otherwise loop i from start to n - need (later positions cannot leave enough elements). Skip i if i > start and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]: at one recursion level a value may be placed in the next slot only once, because a second copy would repeat everything the first copy already produced. A later copy may still be used deeper in the recursion, which is how rows such as [2,2,5] arise.
Each node of the search tree that has enough elements left leads to at least one recorded row, so the time is proportional to the output size times k. The output is at most C(12, 6) = 924 rows.
solution:
def distinctSubsetsOfSize(nums, k):
    nums = sorted(nums)
    n = len(nums)
    res = []
    cur = []

    def go(start, need):
        if need == 0:
            res.append(cur[:])
            return
        for i in range(start, n - need + 1):
            if i > start and nums[i] == nums[i - 1]:
                continue
            cur.append(nums[i])
            go(i + 1, need - 1)
            cur.pop()

    go(0, k)
    return res
